narrative:
The model determined that you have a 29% chance of being a bad credit risk. While this is not an extremely high probability, it was enough for the bank to deny your loan application.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this decision were the purpose of the loan, the status of your checking account, and how long you have lived at your current residence. The fact that you are requesting the loan for business purposes pushed the prediction toward approval. However, this positive effect was outweighed by two other important factors that worked against you.

Your checking account status of 0-200 DM was the strongest single reason for the denial. Most approved applicants either have no checking account or hold substantially more money in theirs, so this limited balance signaled higher risk to the model. Additionally, having lived at your present address for four years also increased the predicted risk. Approved applicants tend to have lived in their current home for a shorter time on average.

Taken together, these factors led the bank to turn down your request. To improve your chances next time, focus on building a larger balance in your checking account before reapplying and consider whether a different loan purpose might be viewed more favorably. You may also want to explore other lenders with different approval criteria.
